host_scope: user-authorized Windows workstation; two sequential repository-owned disposable Win32 fixture processes
question: After bounded recovery on a blocked producer, does the standard compiled public caller refuse the old target generation and independently verify a task effect on a fresh target generation?
correction_from_r07: Add the required single release_all operation to the focus-only stale-generation probe.
Close the continuation fixture using its current task-fixture metadata path.
sequence: Phase 1 repeats the frozen R06 held-SHIFT recovery fault on one owned fixture and must pass before phase 2 starts.
Retire the first supervised session and fixture process; require exit code zero.
Start a distinct fixture process and supervised session; require a different native generation.
Submit one focus-only standard program with exactly one release_all, bound to the old generation; require TARGET_GENERATION_CHANGED and input_dispatched=false.
Observe the new generation through public MCP, then run one compiled caller transition: click x=100,y=60, type office, Ctrl+S, release_all.
Require a post-dispatch observation and an independent server-configured task oracle bound to the exact call, operation and fresh generation.
Verify neutral native readback, clean fixture exit, and foreground restoration.
pass_requires: old fixture retires cleanly before new session input
new fixture PID and target generation differ from old fixture
old-generation probe refusal reason is TARGET_GENERATION_CHANGED with zero input
compiled caller returns exactly one matching action call ID
action release confirmed and native same-generation SHIFT/CTRL/S/left-button readback all up
post-observation capture starts after dispatch response return
fixture event journal has exactly one click, six ordered office character events, and one save
exact effect file and independent verifier receipt match call ID, operation ID and fresh generation
new fixture exits with code zero and foreground is restored
all raw and preregistration files match manifests
limits: The producer fault is injected before native SendInput; it does not simulate an OS/kernel hang.
No AppServer model call, matched efficiency, WSLc allocation, MAP01, or reliability estimate is included.
One trial; first failure is immutable and is not replayed.
